# Disabled

When a control cannot be used yet, or by this person: actions stay enabled and explain, and what a role can never use is hidden.

**Kind:** Pattern

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/storybook-docs/patterns/Disabled/Disabled.mdx`

## The four answers

From most to least often. Disabling is the exception, not the default.

- **Enabled, and it explains.** An action stays pressable and says what is missing when pressed. It disables only while sending.
- **Disabled with a visible reason.** A field or option that waits on a prerequisite the person can fix here. The reason is the caption or the option's description line.
- **Read-only.** Content people must read but cannot change. It has its own pattern.
- **Hidden.** What this role can never use is left out, not dimmed. The one exception is the Toolkit, locked during onboarding and never hidden.

## Key cases

## Usage

Use Disabled when something on the page cannot be used right now. Reach for it last: an enabled action that explains is better than a dimmed one, read-only is better for content people must read, and hiding is right for what a role can never use.

| The situation | Answer | Where the reason goes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A submit with fields missing | Enabled; pressing it marks the fields | Field errors |
| A button while its action sends | Disabled with a spinner in place | None; it is self-evident |
| A field that waits on another field on this screen | Disabled | The caption: "Choose a school first" |
| An option that cannot apply | Disabled | The option's description line |
| A prerequisite that blocks the main action or several items | Disabled, plus a warning `SectionMessage` above | The message says how to turn it on |
| Back on step one; Danger until the name matches | Disabled | None, or the field caption |
| Content this person must read but cannot change | Read-only | The caption |
| An action this role can never take | Hidden | None |
| The Toolkit during onboarding | Locked, visible | The Sidebar line that says what unlocks it |

## Alternatives

- For a value this person cannot change but must read, follow Read-only.
- For what a role can never use, leave the control, page or Sidebar item out.
- For a submit that is not ready, keep it enabled and let validation explain; see Forms.

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Caption: "Choose a school first." | "Disabled", "Not available". |
| Option description: "Ms. Ortiz has a session then." | A faded option with no line. |
| Warning message: "Add a school to this group to schedule sessions." with "Add school". | "Some actions are unavailable." |
| Toolkit: "Complete your assigned training to unlock the Toolkit." | "Locked". |

## Accessibility

- A disabled control leaves the tab order and gets no events; the reason beside it is ordinary text a screen reader reads with the field, tied through the caption.
- The warning `SectionMessage` is announced when it appears.
- Disabled controls fade; the caption keeps full contrast, so the reason stays readable.

## Related

- Read-only: use when the value must be read.
- Forms: use for the enabled submit.
- Common actions: use for the sending button.
- Navigation: use for the Sidebar's locked Toolkit.
- `Button`, `IconButton`, `Select`, `Checkbox`, `RadioGroup`, `DropdownMenu`, `SectionMessage`: the components.

## Best practices

### Keep actions enabled and explain what is missing when pressed. {#keep-actions-enabled-and-explain-what-is-missing-when-pressed}

**Checked:** Automatic

A disabled button gives no direction and leaves the tab order. Pressing an action that cannot run yet marks what is missing. A button disables only while sending. A form's submit follows Forms.

### Disable a field or option only for a prerequisite the person can fix on the same screen. {#disable-a-field-or-option-only-for-a-prerequisite-the-person-can-fix-on-the-same-screen}

**Checked:** Review

Group waits on School; a time slot waits on a date. Anything blocked by something off this screen is enabled and explains, read-only, or hidden.

### Put the reason in visible text where the cause is. {#put-the-reason-in-visible-text-where-the-cause-is}

**Checked:** Automatic

The field caption or the option's description line. When the prerequisite blocks the main action or several items, a warning `SectionMessage` above says how to turn it on. Self-evident cases need no reason: Back on the first step.

### Keep the reason in text on the page, never in a tooltip on a disabled control. {#keep-the-reason-in-text-on-the-page-never-in-a-tooltip-on-a-disabled-control}

**Checked:** Automatic

A disabled control gets no events and is absent on touch, so a tooltip would never open for the people who need it most. A disabled control keeps its default behavior and leaves the tab order.

Do: The reason as the caption: "Choose a school first".
Don't: The reason in a tooltip on a faded field: it never opens on touch.

### Hide what a role can never use. {#hide-what-a-role-can-never-use}

**Checked:** Review

An action a tutor can never take, such as deleting a school, is left out, not dimmed. A breadcrumb level the person cannot open is left out. Only a change of role brings it back.

Do: An action a tutor can never take is left out of the menu.
Don't: A faded "Delete school" that a tutor will never be able to press.

### Lock the Toolkit during onboarding and keep it visible. {#lock-the-toolkit-during-onboarding-and-keep-it-visible}

**Checked:** Review

Tutors see what training unlocks. The Sidebar item shows a lock and a line that says what unlocks it; the line is Planned .

### Make content people must read read-only, not disabled. {#make-content-people-must-read-read-only-not-disabled}

**Checked:** Automatic

Disabled fades and leaves the tab order; read-only stays readable at full contrast. The two are never swapped.
